decision_cruda.rationale: LH-03 is repairable in place, with a likely fix at 09:54 and a high estimate of 10:00. Radio and CMMS agree. The stope holds 323 t at 8.4 g/t, which is more than LH-03 can load before 17:00, so the loss is only about 0.4 h, or roughly 3 oz. A loan would have to travel and would take a loader from a producing stope or a development heading (1.0–1.5 oz/h). It would arrive about when LH-03 is back, so it wouldn't pay. I'm making no moves.

LH-03 is down until about 15:30 (likely) and could be down until 17:30. C590-07 holds 323 t at 8.4 g/t, about 87 oz, and has no loader. The radio and CMMS agree on the failure, so a loan is allowed. LH-08 (LH410, 25.4 t/h) comes from the Norte heading worth 1.0 oz/h. It takes 0.67 h to arrive and then loads about 5.8 h, which is roughly 147 t or 39 oz. The heading loses about 6.3 oz, so the net gain is about 33 oz. LH-09 would cost 1.5 oz/h, which nets about 30 oz even with its shorter 0.35 h trip. Central's stockpile is 170 of 450 t. Inflow would be about 108 t/h against truck capacity of 91 t/h, a surplus of about 17 t/h, or about 100 t over 6 h. That fits in the 280 t of free space. Reserves cannot be activated because no stope has stopped.
